title: Sports radio to try in Malta
intro: Radio snapshot for 13–19 October 2026. The clearest English-language sports lead is a “Sports Channel” service that one specialist directory labels “(Talk Sport)” on block 6C (185.360 MHz) while the industry multiplex table places a service of that name on block 12A and the operator’s own list shows none — block disputed, scan by name: talkSPORT is an official Premier League audio broadcaster, so this is the first receiver scan to try on 17–18 October 2026. What the Malta relay actually carries, and its indoor reception, are unverified. Malta’s block 6A carries BBC World Service (Sportsworld, dated 17–18 October episodes, general live sport) plus Rai Radio Uno/Due/Tre, NET FM and Vibe HD; Vibe FM is the published radio partner of the Malta Premier League. The six BBC Radio 5 Live / 5 Sports Extra episode JSON records name seven UK Premier League commentaries across 17–18 October (including Bournemouth–Sunderland on 5 Sports Extra 2), with the page-vs-JSON service labels resolved via episode cross-reference texts — still UK-only schedule evidence. Kalshi’s own help centre says trading from many countries and while travelling abroad is possible subject to its Member Agreement, while third-party guidance conflicts; eligibility stays account-specific. No named-event carriage was verified.

records.description: NET FM is listed by the Broadcasting Authority at FM 101 MHz, and the station’s own schedule page was read in full on 11 October 2026. It publishes three weekend sports-branded slots: Friday 18:30 “Mhux Premier biss” (“Not just the Premier League”), Saturday 16:00 “Hits & Score” and Sunday 15:00 “Sports Box”. The Saturday and Sunday slots coincide exactly with the Malta-time kick-off windows of the Premier League fixtures scheduled that weekend (most Saturday 16:00 and Sunday 15:00 fixtures), which is a testable planning lead — but the station publishes only a recurring weekly grid, with no dated 17–18 October running order and no promise of live commentary on any named match. Programmes and continuity are largely in Maltese. The grid does not state a time zone explicitly; Malta local time is the reasonable reading and the station broadcasts locally.
records.notes: Station grid read 11 October 2026: https://netfm.com.mt/ . Frequency from the Broadcasting Authority licensed-stations list: https://ba.org.mt/stations-licenced . NET FM is also listed as a DAB+ channel by the Malta DAB+ operator: https://dab.com.mt/channels/ . The listener should recheck the station’s live page on 16–18 October: a recurring grid is not a dated schedule and the sports slots may be discussion programming rather than commentary. No on-location reception test was possible. The station also offers an internet stream, which is not broadcast radio. Second-session additions: the station is also carried on Malta DAB+ block 6A (181.936 MHz) under the service name “Net FM”, per the specialist station list read 11 October 2026: https://radioinmalta.com/en/dab/6a.php — a second tuning route if the FM signal is weak indoors. No carriage of the Thunderpick event, the Gżira United–Mosta fixture or the Rolex Middle Sea Race was confirmed. The grid does not state its time zone.

records.description: WorldDAB lists BBC World Service on Malta’s Digi B Network, Band III block 6A at 181.936 MHz, and the Malta DAB+ operator’s own channel directory separately lists BBC World Service. The BBC’s own institutional listening page states that in Malta BBC World Service can be heard 24 hours a day on the DAB+ service and that a DAB+ radio purchased in Malta is necessary, because DAB radios purchased in the UK operate on a different codec. That is a broadcaster statement about carriage and receiver type, not a measured signal-strength result, and it says nothing about Premier League commentary: BBC World Service’s sport output is general live sport, and its UK football commentary services are separate stations. Second session, 11 October 2026: the same Multiplexes table places BBC WS on Digi B Network, block 6A at 181.936 MHz; a specialist directory additionally lists transmission sites at Għargħur and Żebbuġ (Gozo) — https://www.wohnort.org/dab/malta.html — but that is a directory, not an on-location reception test.

records.description: Three listings agree that a service called “Sports Channel” is carried on Malta DAB+: the specialist Radio in Malta directory names it “Sports Channel (Talk Sport)” on block 6C, WorldDAB’s Multiplexes table lists a regular “Sports Channel” service on Digi B 2, block 12A, and Wikipedia’s talkSPORT article lists “DAB+: 6C (Malta)” among the station’s frequencies. talkSPORT is an official English Premier League audio broadcaster and the league’s global audio partner, which makes this the most promising lead for English live football commentary on a radio in Malta during the 17–18 October fixture window. What is unresolved is bigger than signal strength: the two directories disagree on which block carries the service, and the Maltese DAB+ operator’s own channel list (read in full on 11 October 2026) lists no such service at all. The relay could therefore be a talkSPORT simulcast, a different sports service reusing the name, or absent. Scan by service name and listen before trusting it.
records.notes: Specialist directory read 11 October 2026: https://radioinmalta.com/en/dab/6c.php gives 185.360 MHz, allotment MLT00018, on air since 2012, and lists “Sports Channel (Talk Sport)” at 32 kbps HE-AAC v2 among UK relays (LBC 97.3, Capital, Gold, Smooth, Jazz FM) and Maltese services. WorldDAB’s Multiplexes table lists a “Sports Channel” regular DAB+ service on Digi B 2, block 12A (223.936 MHz): https://www.worlddab.org/why-dab-plus/countries/malta/multiplexes . The operator’s own channel directory lists no sports service: https://dab.com.mt/channels/ . Wikipedia’s talkSPORT article lists “DAB+: 6C (Malta)”: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talksport . Rights context: https://www.premierleague.com/en/about/partners/talksport . Keep this record unverified: block, service identity, schedule and reception are all unconfirmed.

records.name: Malta DAB+ tuning guide — blocks 6A, 6C and 12A
records.area: Malta and Gozo (national Digi B multiplexes); indoor reception varies by building
records.address: Not applicable — technical tuning data; scan by service name on a DAB+ receiver
records.hours: Not a schedule. Published block data: 6A 181.936 MHz (allotment MLT00017, on air since July 2008, transmitters Għargħur 10 kW and Żebbuġ, Gozo); 6C 185.360 MHz (allotment MLT00018, on air since 2012); 12A 223.936 MHz (Digi B 2).
records.description: Malta has used DAB+ (not older DAB) since 2008, with national coverage from the Digi B Network multiplexes on blocks 6A, 6C and 12A, so a DAB+-compatible receiver is required and should find the services by name rather than by dial frequency. Practical split for this trip: block 6A carries BBC World Service, Rai Radio Uno/Due/Tre, Net FM, Vibe HD and most Maltese services; block 6C carries UK relays such as LBC 97.3, Capital, Gold, Smooth and Jazz FM plus several Italian services, and the specialist directory also lists a “Sports Channel (Talk Sport)” there — though the industry multiplex table places a “Sports Channel” on block 12A instead, and the operator’s own channel list shows no sports service, so scan both blocks. A one-touch scan of the three blocks is the fastest way to answer the radio question in Malta itself.
records.notes: Block and station data read 11 October 2026 from the Radio in Malta DAB+ pages: https://radioinmalta.com/en/dab/ , https://radioinmalta.com/en/dab/6a.php and https://radioinmalta.com/en/dab/6c.php . Corroborated by WorldDAB’s Malta country page and multiplex table (multiplexes operated by Digi B Network; coverage via 6A/6C/12A): https://www.worlddab.org/countries/malta and https://www.worlddab.org/countries/malta/multiplexes , and by the MCA’s DAB+ consultation frequency table: https://www.mca.org.mt/sites/default/files/MCA-C-21-4261%20-%20DAB%20Plus%20Consultation_0.pdf . Radio in Malta is a specialist enthusiast directory and WorldDAB is an industry association, so both are directory evidence, not the Maltese network operator’s live data: service names, bit rates and block contents can change, and reception inside a seafront hotel or a metal-framed studio building was not measured. Verify by scanning on arrival; the station list is not a programme guide.
records.price range: Broadcast reception is free; a DAB+ receiver is required (hardware not priced here). A pocket DAB+ receiver or a phone with a DAB+ accessory is the lightest option for a trip

records.name: What radio hardware actually works in Malta (US traveller)
records.area: Malta — national FM and DAB+ coverage
records.hours: Check before departure; a receiver bought locally removes the codec risk
records.price range: Not published here; local receiver prices were not checked
records.description: Three separate compatibility questions decide what a US traveller can actually listen to. 1) Analog FM travels: Maltese national FM stations sit inside the international FM broadcast band, which the ITU GE84 plan sets at 87.5–108 MHz for Region 1. Check the tuning range printed on any receiver before relying on it, and remember most phone radios are disabled. 2) DAB+ is not what US equipment decodes: the United States adopted HD Radio, a different digital standard, and DAB/DAB+ receivers and HD Radio receivers cannot decode each other’s signals. The BBC’s own guidance adds that even UK DAB radios will not work in Malta because of a different codec, and that a DAB+ radio purchased in Malta is the correct device. 3) A phone app or web stream is not broadcast radio: it depends on mobile data, roaming cost and any territory limits, and it should not be counted as an over-the-air radio option.
records.notes: BBC institutional listening page (Malta DAB+ carriage and the “DAB+ radio purchased in Malta is necessary… UK DAB radios operate on a different codec” wording): https://www.bbc.co.uk/worldservice/mobile/institutional/2009/03/000000_digitallisting.shtml . ITU workshop material giving the Region 1 FM broadcast band as 87.5–108 MHz under the GE84 Agreement: https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-R/terrestrial/workshops/SRME-19/Documents/Workshop/SRME-19-DigitalRadio.pdf . Encyclopaedia reference for the HD Radio/DAB+ incompatibility: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HD_Radio . WorldDAB Malta multiplexes: https://www.worlddab.org/why-dab-plus/countries/malta/multiplexes . The third point is a practical caution, not a sourced claim about a specific app. No receiver was tested in Malta.
